input: Find a reliable accountant for self-employment taxes

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user needs one-time tax filing help, ongoing quarterly tax planning, bookkeeping, or full financial advisory changes which type of accountant to look for and what services to request.

The complexity of the user's self-employment situation (sole proprietor, LLC, S-corp, multiple income streams, employees) determines what level of expertise and specialization is required in an accountant.
Whether the user needs a local in-person accountant or is open to remote/online services significantly affects the search method and available options.
Budget for accountant fees will determine whether they look at CPA firms, independent accountants, or lower-cost services, and how much ongoing support is realistic.
The user may have strong preferences around industry-specific experience (e.g., freelance creative vs. contractor vs. consultant), which narrows the field considerably.
Understanding what 'reliable' means to this user — e.g., proactive communication, audit support, specific credentials like CPA or EA — shapes how to evaluate and shortlist candidates.
Knowing the user's timeline (e.g., tax deadline approaching, just starting out) determines urgency and whether they need someone immediately available or can take time to vet options carefully.

gold.taskTitle: Find a reliable accountant for self-employment taxes
gold.taskDescription: Identify and hire a trustworthy accountant who can handle tax filing and/or planning for a self-employed individual.

questions.title: What services do you need — filing, planning, or ongoing bookkeeping?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user needs a one-time tax filing, quarterly estimated tax planning, year-round bookkeeping support, or a combination of these services.

questions.title: How is your self-employment structured — sole proprietor, LLC, or S-corp?
questions.description: Determine the legal and financial complexity of the user's self-employment setup to identify the right level of accountant expertise needed.

questions.title: Do you need someone local in person, or is remote working fine?
questions.description: Establish whether geographic proximity is important to the user, which directly affects where and how to search for candidates.

questions.title: What is your approximate budget for accountant fees per year?
questions.description: Understand the financial constraints so the plan can target appropriately priced professionals, from solo CPAs to larger firms.

questions.title: What industry or type of work do you want the accountant experienced in?
questions.description: Identify whether the user works in a niche field (e.g., freelance tech, creative arts, real estate, consulting) where specialized tax knowledge would be a strong advantage.

questions.title: What credentials or qualities matter most to you in an accountant?
questions.description: Find out whether the user prioritizes specific credentials (CPA, EA), proactive communication, audit defense support, or other qualities to define what 'reliable' means for their vetting criteria.

questions.title: How soon do you need the accountant ready to work with you?
questions.description: Determine the urgency of the search — for example, whether a tax deadline is imminent or the user has time to carefully evaluate multiple candidates.
